items.section: 4.1 Living and non-living — a virus and a prion
items.sentence: inert apart from a host, as a spore or a seed is inert
items.text: Within one dry seed two inward societies part by what is seen: among 30-month seeds all germinate, among 66-month seeds the autophagy-mutant ones germinate under 20% and the wild over 60%, in 80-month mutant endosperm over 80% of cells are dead against under 10% in the wild, and with the coat taken off the mutant embryos grow; a freed-marker ratio runs 1.00, 2.30 and 2.77 at 5, 48 and 60 months.
items.from: ### Old dry seeds, with autophagy and with none

items.section: 4.1 Living and non-living — a virus and a prion
items.sentence: inert apart from a host, as a spore or a seed is inert
items.text: Single spores given 3-minute pulses of 10 millimolar L-alanine 2 hours apart stay dormant about 95% after the first pulse, and about half of the rest germinate after the second (52.1% ± 6.2%); a peripheral dye jumps in electrochemical potential at each pulse while the brightness reading holds steady, and a spore that stays dormant stays so for at least 20 further hours.
items.from: ### Dormant spores, at pulses each too small

items.section: 8.1 Hard problems at biology, disequilibrating
items.sentence: meets an aversive stimulus with regular intervals, and slows its movement each time
items.text: A plasmodium fed six days on oat gel with 50 millimolar salt, dried to a sclerotium, held a month and wetted again, crosses a salt bridge 94 of 100 against 54 of 98 for the plain-fed, with more sodium held in the salt-fed plasmodia and their sclerotia, and more sodium even in sclerotia formed with no salt.
items.from: ### A slime mould after a month as a sclerotium

items.section: 8.1 Hard problems at biology, disequilibrating
items.sentence: regenerating worm reacquires conditioned response faster than a naive one
items.text: Planarians made familiar with a rough dish feed sooner than others at four days and at twelve to fifteen; worms with heads cut off and grown again over seven to nine days, tested with no further session, feed no sooner to a measure the reading accepts, and only after one further session of feeding do they feed sooner than regrown worms made familiar with nothing.
items.from: ### Learning after a head's regrowing

items.section: 3.4 Hand goes both ways, and observing homochirality as a sway
items.sentence: a field's own programmes predicting it viable, and no one making it yet
items.text: A polymerase built of amino acids of the other hand lengthens primers of other-hand DNA on other-hand templates and writes RNA of the other hand; a larger one writes the three ribosomal RNAs whole in the other hand and outlasts an enzyme of the living hand; and in two meteorites amino acids rare in living things hold an excess of the living hand — each a molecule of the other hand made by makers of the living hand, with a living self of its own origin at the other hand observed at none and looked for.
items.from: ### Polymerases of the other hand, and a living hand looked for

items.section: 7.2 Ageing — the sway no longer coming round again
items.sentence: Ageing is that sway coming round again with a narrower range each cycle
items.text: Across 16 mammal species the somatic mutation rate in a year runs inversely with lifespan, about 47 substitutions in a genome a year in humans against about 796 in mice, while the burden at the end of lifespan varies only about threefold across about thirtyfold in lifespan, near 3,200 substitutions in a crypt; the giraffe and the naked mole-rat, about twenty-three-thousand-fold apart in body mass, hold near-equal rates, 99 and 93 a year, and near-equal lifespans, 24 and 25 years.
items.from: ### Somatic changes across sixteen mammals' lifespans

items.section: 4.5 Circadian clock — changing and changing back, making a beat
items.sentence: two beats with close paces join across
items.text: Pairs of embryonic heart-cell aggregates beating at different rates, brought into contact, come to one beat, and the latency between their joined beats runs linearly with the coupling resistance between them, 3.7 milliseconds for each megohm at 4.8 millimolar potassium and 10.1 at 1.3 millimolar.
items.from: ### Two heart-cell aggregates coming to one beat

items.section: Droplets
items.text: In budding yeast with one extra chromosome, protein amounts largely scale with gene copy number, yet about a fifth of the proteins from the extra chromosome are held down, most of them parts of multiprotein complexes, while their messages rise about 1.9-fold — a part of a complex reaches a stable fold only as it joins its complex, and the rest breaks down.
items.from: ### Dosage at an extra chromosome in yeast

items.section: 6.5 Generational chain
items.text: Epigenetic age read by methylation clocks falls through early embryogenesis and rises after, its lowest point lying between embryonic days 4.5 and 10.5 and near days 6.5 to 7.5, about the time of gastrulation, with most prenatal readings in a related animal rising or holding.
items.from: ### Epigenetic age falling in the early embryo

items.section: 5.1 Conception — two selves conceiving a third
items.sentence: identical twins are one conceiving going on as two selves, an embryo re-resolving to two wholes, each unique with its own same-existing from parting on
items.text: A looser inner cell mass is more likely to part, with physical forces from blastocoel formation or 8-shaped hatching, and transfer of a single embryo does not prevent identical twins; the move that opens and bounds identical twinning stands unresolved.
items.from: ### The initiating of identical twinning, unexplained

items.section: 5.1 Conception — two selves conceiving a third
items.sentence: And one sperm's fusing closes coupling to others
items.text: The egg's receptor for a sperm surface protein is shed rapidly from the egg surface after fusing; sperm lacking one phospholipase induce fewer, smaller calcium spikes, 2.75 against 12.0, and entry by more than one sperm rises to 82.4% against 7.6% when the surface closing comes late.
items.from: ### Calcium oscillations and Juno at mouse eggs

items.section: 5.1 Conception — two selves conceiving a third
items.sentence: Then two haploid gametes fuse with fertilization — two selves' halving codes going to one diploid zygote
items.text: In the zygote two separate bipolar spindles form, one gathering each parent's genome, the two aligning so the genomes lie side by side and stay apart through the first division and mix only in the later divisions; spindles failing to align give a two-cell embryo with binucleated cells.
items.from: ### Two parental genomes apart through the first division

items.section: 5.2 A self recursioning into a new form — development and metamorphosis
items.text: A cytoplasmic clock keeps the same period as the division cycle and goes on with no nucleus; the early embryo runs 12 rapid synchronous cleavages and then slower asynchronous ones, the turn to the slower set standing apart from cell division, from the time since fertilization and from any numbering of DNA marks, and placed instead at a ratio of nuclear material to cytoplasm.
items.from: ### An egg's cycle with no nucleus, and its transition

items.section: 4.5 Circadian clock — changing and changing back, making a beat
items.sentence: Nearly every living thing has a clock
items.text: The heart's own beat opens about the third week after conception; a fetus and a newborn make no melatonin of their own and the mother's melatonin passes to the fetus, an overt daily rhythm in melatonin and cortisol opens only after birth, a sleep-wake rhythm by about 5 weeks and consolidating near 15 weeks, and a mother and her three-month-old settle their heart rhythms within lags under one second during shared affect.
items.from: ### The conceived's beat and day opening later

items.section: 4.5 Circadian clock — changing and changing back, making a beat
items.sentence: self-sustaining, going on on its own even with no light to cue it
items.text: In constant darkness the daily opening and closing of leaves goes on; a cyanobacterial clock rebuilt in a tube from three proteins with added fuel holds a 22-hour rhythm over several days; and a blind cavefish isolated beneath the desert holds a food-settled rhythm near 47 hours at 22 degrees, 43 at 25 and 38 at 29, with no light setting it.
items.from: ### Daily rhythms continuing with no day arriving

items.section: 4.6 Photosynthesis and respiration — the six sharing with the six
items.sentence: Living engine turns as two coupling cycles, each sharing with the other its input
items.text: Isolated chloroplasts given short flashes after darkness yield most oxygen on the third flash and less on the fourth, the yield repeating in a cycle of four that damps over about three to four cycles; and seeds given alternating red and far-red flashes answer only to the last flash, opening after a red one and resting after a far-red one.
items.from: ### Oxygen at each fourth flash, and the last flash's colour

items.section: 4.6 Photosynthesis and respiration — the six sharing with the six
items.sentence: Living engine turns as two coupling cycles, each sharing with the other its input
items.text: Light beyond 680 nanometres alone drives photosynthesis slowly, and with shorter-wavelength light given together with it the rate exceeds the sum of the two rates apart — a +1 of two colours taken together that neither gives alone.
items.from: ### Two colours together at a leaf

items.section: 4.5 Circadian clock — changing and changing back, making a beat

items.text: A potato tuber lays starch growth rings that go on in constant conditions, while a tree's yearly earlywood and latewood and a cereal endosperm's starch rings follow day and night.
items.from: ### Starch rings continuing in constant conditions

items.section: 5.1 Conception — two selves conceiving a third
items.sentence: fraternal twins are two conceivings with one coupling, two thirds, each a +1 of its own coupling
items.text: Hares conceive a second litter days 37 to 41 into a 42-day pregnancy, early embryos lying in the oviduct beside full fetuses in the uterus and taking hold after the birth, in 54.4% of the pregnancies where it is possible, raising a season's output from 14.4 to 19.5 young — two conceivings in one female parted in time.
items.from: ### A second conception late in a hare's pregnancy

items.section: 5.1 Conception — two selves conceiving a third
items.sentence: fraternal twins are two conceivings with one coupling, two thirds, each a +1 of its own coupling
items.text: Two eggs of one cycle fertilised by two sperm give fraternal twins of two fathers, about 2.4% of fraternal twins in contested cases; and two eggs each fertilised, aggregating at the early embryo, give one person of two zygotes whose cell groups each hold their own makeup.
items.from: ### Two fathers at one cycle; two zygotes one person
